title: 3B N-Gram Table
description: Schema for n-gram-table.json - the machine-readable LLM Collation Table a single podcast episode produces at one scope (Topic Only / Location / Extension). The JSON has three top-level members: a `content` block (the table itself - four-column row set, scope, location, counts, dedup, localization result), a generated `research_summary` text field (the plain-language Executive Summary lead paragraph), and an `internal` block. The `internal` block carries two kinds of content: (a) the four review-tier blocks that render under the Doc's bottom `INTERNAL` H1 in a locked order - Cluster Architecture, Topic Entities, Local Anchors, Bridge Entity Coverage; and (b) provenance / metadata (topic, industry, jurisdiction, episode, version, created, parent anchor, skill, run provenance) plus the pipe-delimited metadata header line, which by contract NEVER render into the Doc and live in the JSON `internal` block + metadata.json only. The `content` block, `research_summary`, and the four `internal` review-tier blocks are what render into the client-facing Google Doc; the `internal` provenance/metadata fields do not.

research_summary.description: The generated plain-language narrative paragraph that leads the client-facing Executive Summary section (heading -> this paragraph -> stat bullets). Generated per run, jargon-free, client-facing. Names the top recurring entities, states they recur whenever the topic is searched and discussed, frames the jurisdictional picture (local roads / hospitals / courts / agencies; Topic Only scope drops the local framing and notes comprehensive coverage instead), and ties to the N planned questions in plain terms.

StringOrStringArray.description: Either a single string or an array of strings. The skill writes column cells in either form depending on how many items the row carries.

Content.description: The n-gram table content - everything that renders into the client-facing Google Doc body.

scope.description: The episode scope this table was generated at. Governs entity form, acronym convention, separator, and per-row entity count. Maps to the three-field geo model: a Location / Extension scope is the Episode geo target (the one city this table emphasizes); Topic Only carries no episode geo target. Distinct from the Optimization scope (show anchor) - the show-wide breadth the upstream research was gathered at, which is not a field on this table.

location.description: Jurisdiction label = the Episode geo target city this table is built to rank for (geo-model field 3). Required when scope is Location or Extension. Format: 'CA', 'CA - Los Angeles County', or 'CA - Long Beach'. No colons, dashes only.

row_count.description: Final row count after the dedup pass. Topic Only / Location target 25-35; Extension is 10.

entities_per_row_avg.description: Average count of entities per row across the table. Reported in the client-facing Executive Summary stat bullets.

dedup_merges.description: Dedup pass result. Either an integer count of merges performed, or an array of merge records (each describing the question pair folded together).

items.description: A single dedup merge: the weaker question folded into the survivor.

localization_scan_result.description: Result of the localization scan. PASS or FAIL when scope is Location/Extension; N/A when scope is Topic Only (scan does not apply).

rows.description: The four-column collation rows. Every row carries a question and its n-grams, entities, and predicates.

Row.description: One row of the collation table.

question_text.description: The on-air question, phrased conversationally the way a co-host would ask it.

ngrams.description: N-grams to mention. 3-5 per row - a mix of high-intent, long-tail, and process-oriented phrases.

entities.description: Entities to mention. Real-world named orgs only, drawn from the matching-scope entity map. Per-row count, acronym convention, and separator vary by scope.

predicates.description: Predicates to mention. 3-5 per row - action verb phrases describing what a practitioner does.

QuestionRefList.description: An ordered list of 1-based question numbers (Q-refs) from the collation table. Used by the Cluster Architecture and Bridge Entity Coverage blocks to map a pillar / bridge entity back to the questions it covers.

GroupedEntityBlock.description: A grouped-by-type entity block. Each key is a type sub-label (e.g. 'Accident Types', 'Law Enforcement') and each value is the array of entity names under that type. Renders in the Doc as a section heading, then per type a bold sub-label followed by a bullet list. The Topic Entities and Local Anchors INTERNAL blocks both use this identical shape.

Internal.description: Internal block. Carries TWO kinds of content: (1) the four review-tier blocks that DO render under the bottom `INTERNAL` H1 of the client-facing Doc - `cluster_architecture`, `topic_entities`, `local_anchors`, `bridge_entity_coverage`, in that locked order; and (2) provenance / metadata fields (topic, industry, jurisdiction, episode, version, created, parent_anchor, skill, run provenance) plus the pipe-delimited metadata header - which by contract NEVER render into the Doc and live in the JSON `internal` block + metadata.json only. The four review-tier blocks are derived from the collation table itself. `local_anchors` is present only at Location / Extension scope; it is an empty object for Topic Only scope.

cluster_architecture.description: INTERNAL block 1 - the thematic pillars. Each key is a pillar name and each value is the list of question numbers (Q-refs) that fall under it. The lead block of the INTERNAL section. Always present, every scope.

topic_entities.description: INTERNAL block 2 - the universal, practice-area entities (accident types, injury types, legal standards / statutes, damages concepts, agencies, and other non-local entities), grouped by type. Always present, every scope. Same grouped-by-type shape as `local_anchors`.

local_anchors.description: INTERNAL block 3 - the jurisdiction-specific entities (Roads / Highways, Law Enforcement, Medical Providers, Courts, County / Municipal), grouped by type. Present only at Location / Extension scope; an empty object {} for Topic Only scope. Same grouped-by-type shape as `topic_entities`.

bridge_entity_coverage.description: INTERNAL block 4 - the cross-cutting bridge entities (those recurring across multiple questions) mapped to the question numbers they appear in. Each key is an entity name and each value is its list of Q-refs. Always present, every scope; may be an empty object when no entity recurs across enough questions.

topic.description: Practice area / topic. Internal metadata header field.

industry.description: Top-level industry (Legal, Healthcare, Finance, etc.). Internal metadata header field.

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction the table is built for, or 'N/A' for Topic Only scope. Internal metadata header field.

episode.description: Episode title. Internal metadata header field.

version.description: Version of this n-gram table. Internal metadata header field.

created.description: ISO date the table was created. Internal metadata header field.

parent_anchor.description: The parent anchor episode this table inherits from, or 'N/A' when this is the anchor. Internal metadata header field.

skill.description: The skill that produced this table. Internal metadata header field.

run_date.description: ISO date the table was generated this run.

entity_map_source.description: Where the upstream entity map was read from. 'local' = local Desktop deliverables path; 'drive' = shared Drive at matching scope.

entity_map_path.description: Path to the upstream entity-map.json the table was built against.

references_status.description: Whether the bundled references/examples were used as calibration anchors. 'used' = at least one example read; 'empty' = examples file empty, ran on in-skill methodology alone.

content_plan.description: Whether a content plan (= topic plan, pod-2A-topic-planner output) was found at the per-client Topic Plan slot.

schema_status.description: Whether this schema file was present and validated against at run time. 'validated' = present and checked; 'missing' = schema file absent, validation skipped.
